purpose: Ribociclib is used to treat certain types of breast cancer that are hormone receptor-positive (HR+) and HER2-negative. It is typically used in combination with another hormone-blocking medicine. It can be used in adults with early-stage or advanced/metastatic breast cancer.
how_it_works: Cancer cells grow by dividing over and over again. Ribociclib works by blocking specific proteins in cancer cells — called CDK4 and CDK6 — that act like an 'on switch' for cell division. By blocking these proteins, the medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from multiplying.
common_side_effects: Low blood cell counts (which can increase infection risk or cause fatigue), nausea, tiredness, hair thinning, diarrhea, headache, low white blood cell counts (neutropenia), and abnormal liver blood tests. Your doctor will monitor your blood regularly.
warnings: Ribociclib can cause a serious heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation, which can be life-threatening — your doctor will check your heart with an EKG before and during treatment. It can also cause serious liver problems, so liver function tests will be monitored. It can harm an unborn baby, so use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as many drugs can interact with ribociclib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 600 mg (three 200 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day for 21 days, followed by 7 days off — making a 28-day cycle. It is taken at the same time each day, with or without food. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects.
